episodes.title: Jensen Huang Is Back + AI Solves the Riemann Hypothesis
episodes.about: Jensen Huang is back at the helm of Nvidia after the board received input from 'senior levels' of the U.S. government; Kevin Roose and Casey Newton get into the roles Trump and JD Vance played, how much of it is about the stock market, and why those celebrating his return might reconsider. Then Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpoge says he and Claude proved the Riemann hypothesis, a problem open since 1859: how mathematicians are reacting, and how many other domains might see the same acceleration. Plus three AI talking points for the Thanksgiving table.
episodes.why: Always-include show. Huang is back at Nvidia after White House pressure, and an Anthropic mathematician says he and Claude proved the Riemann hypothesis — Roose and Newton work through both stories and the math world's reaction.

episodes.title: The Revolution vs The Renaissance — Thariq Shihipar, OpenAI
episodes.about: AI can make software cheap enough to produce by the thousand and still give you more time to make one thing feel right. Recorded at AI Engineer CODE, OpenAI's Thariq Shihipar shows how those two futures — the Revolution and the Renaissance — can coexist, demoing it on his own fighting game, where he edits the size of a rock in the scene.
episodes.why: OpenAI's Thariq Shihipar argues cheap, abundant code and slow, careful craft are not opposites — making software by the thousand can buy back the time to make one thing feel right.

episodes.title: Dual proofs of legendary Riemann hypothesis stun mathematicians
episodes.about: Mathematicians are astounded by dual proofs of the Riemann hypothesis — one AI-assisted, one human-written — for a problem that has stood since 1859, and Nature charts how AI shocks are rattling the next generation of mathematicians. Plus research highlights (weight training versus muscle loss on obesity drugs; a dinosaur's rest break) and what the collapse of COP31 means for climate plans.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — Nature Podcast is the journal Nature's science show, new here; the mathematicians' own account of the dual Riemann proofs, plus data on how AI is rattling the field's next generation.

episodes.title: Can AI show us how language works? | Jennifer Hu
episodes.about: Language is central to nearly every moment of our lives, yet researchers know surprisingly little about how it works. Computational cognitive scientist Jennifer Hu uses AI models as a new kind of lab for studying how humans learn language, showing where machines succeed, where they stumble — and what those results reveal about our own minds.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — TED Talks Daily is the daily TED talk feed, new here; Jennifer Hu uses language models as a lab for how children learn language, and the places the models fail are the informative part.

episodes.title: AI food slop is on the menu
episodes.about: It's the time of year when everyone has food on the brain — glistening turkeys, steaming pies — but increasingly those images look a bit off, thanks to AI. From Marketplace Tech's 'Uncanny AI' series: Brady Brickner-Wood wrote about AI food images for The New Yorker; the worst examples, he says, can look sweaty, unnaturally fractal, almost insect-like.
episodes.why: Seven minutes, out this morning: AI-generated food photos are taking over menus and ads, and the New Yorker's writer on the beat explains why they look sweaty and fractal up close.
